issues.description: Method SealSaloon.calculateTotalPrice(Meal): The problem statement (UML and explanatory text) specifies calculateTotalPrice should return a double to allow precise financial calculations, but the reference implementation in src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java declares calculateTotalPrice as returning an int and returns an integer sum. This mismatch between the specified return type (double) and the implemented return type (int) can confuse students about the expected numeric type and precision for price calculations and may lead to inconsistent student implementations or failing style/precision checks.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent with the problem statement. Update the method signature in SealSaloon.java to public static double calculateTotalPrice(Meal meal) and change the implementation to accumulate and return a double (e.g., double sum = 0.0; sum += ingredient.getPrice(); return sum;). Update the template/solution call sites if necessary. Alternatively, if integer prices are intended, update the problem statement/UML to specify an int return type and remove the reference to double precision.
